title: HTTP transport alias in recurring frontend endpoint export
fault_primitive: Recurring EndpointSlice export binds the frontend HTTP port name to the discovery administration transport and peer inventory
incident_class: Operational service-discovery export retains an incompatible transport mapping after a naming migration
symptoms: Intermittent connection refusals and HTTP 404 responses affect hotel operations. Native frontend pods, Deployment, Service selector, targetPort, and legacy Endpoints remain healthy. Consul receives unrelated hotel URLs, and the existing frontend TCP endpoint alert fires.
why_hard: The externally managed slice has the correct frontend service-name label and Service owner identity. Native Endpoints and direct Pod checks remain healthy. Deleting the inconsistent slice gives immediate recovery, but a periodic export running inside an existing application container recreates it after two minutes. The export is absent from Deployment and ConfigMap inventories and runs in recommendation, away from the frontend and Consul symptoms. Rollback, frontend replacement, and moderate scaling leave it active. A live wrong HTTP listener retains connections rather than allowing retries to converge on the working frontend.
expected_agent_pitfalls: Trusting healthy legacy Endpoints as the complete routing inventory
Treating Consul's unrelated URL warnings as a client discovery or HTTP API problem
Replacing frontend pods or rolling back an unchanged Deployment
Checking only slice service-name labels and ownerReferences, which agree
Accepting a successful direct pod request or a small sample of successful frontend requests
Deleting the slice and accepting temporary recovery before the next two-minute export
Searching only Deployment and ConfigMap state for the writer of a recurring EndpointSlice
Restarting Consul because it logs unrelated frontend URLs
mitigation_summary: Inspect live application process state to stop the recurring frontend EndpointSlice exporter, remove its namespace-scoped write authority, and remove frontend slices whose membership or transport ports disagree with the live Service selector and Pod ports. No saved manifests or private recovery values are used.
